items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: They had Little Broadway Rastus, who was a terrific drummer. They speak of him.

ctx.x: act, a compact hour act. But they generally did, like twenty minutes or thirty minutes on the Orpheum and the Pantages circuit. It was considered one of the greatest acts. And especially when you mention this name of Florence Mills. She later became one of the greatest Black performers there ever was. And you mention her in awe when you say "Florence Mills." She lit up a stage. She had this charisma that people have, when you see them they just upset a stage, and it's natural. That was Florence Mills.

That was the Tennessee Ten. They had Little Broadway Rastus, who was a terrific drummer. They speak of him. He went to Europe and stayed over there. He could run and jump and slide, slide and sort of... It was mystifying how he could run across the stage and slide, and made a spread eagle on the stage, and just continued to move. When you'd look at the momentum to think he had stopped, he'd slide some more.
